Content:
Rejections are common. Everyone gets it. Recently I got rejected for  'teaching' a recorded course in Data Science.
And the reason is - I faltered during the demo.

During my introspection, I realized that I am not a garden mower to work seamlessly and then come back after a week and mow again.

I am a driller of an oil rig. I dig in depth. When I teach concepts, I aim at 100% of students understanding from zero. Only when you go to depth, you need not revise again for every interview - my belief
So a driller takes breaks and it pauses as well. But once a hole is made, its only another hole pending.

Content:
A piece of wisdom for aspirants lured by/looking for placement Assistance / Guarantee 

Many aspirants tell me they chose the insititute which provides placement assistance/guarantee. And after 3 months, of course, they bash the institute if they don't get placed. From my experience, I can tell you, all they give you is the email to send your CV. Nothing more. Just studying at their institute doesn't give an edge. 

Let's say I am recruiting for an AI team. The Institute approaches me with a pool of students so I am glad to consider . I still expect the same or 'even more' when you come through the institute.  I look at your expertise to code, depth of concepts and go-get attitude. For most recruiters, this matters.  Even if the institute owns the company, they still look at your capability. So work on improving the capability.  

The only favor they do is to get the job openings in front of you. The institute teaches you how to scrap the web and you still depend on them for assistance when you can scrap the web for openings or much more.  Your dependency is a rejection. Simple !!

Content:
I classify work of a data scientist into two parts.  The work done before target variable and the work done after target variable. 
Let me explain
The work after target variable :
    This is what you do everywhere. You get data,problem statement well defined,  you clean it, visualise it, find correlations,take care of outliers, explore all models, create new features, iterate and get best accuracy.
 The MOOCs, kaggle competitions, hackathons, everything you see makes you good at 'after target variable work'

The work before target variable. 
   Organisations capture a large chunks of data and higher management realise that they are sitting on gold mine of data. Now it's the data scientist who has to get into business shoes and make sense of data, design a problem statement , decide a target variable ,pull out required data and get a business proposal 
I see today's data scientist don't practise the 'before target variable' work but this is what makes money for a industry. You may argue that this is the work of 'business roles' or 'managers' but NO. Only you have the idea of models and  if you can do 'before target variable' work too, you become more versatile and you will be invaluable to organisation.

"Data Science in R"  or "Data Science in Python" or "Machine Learning in R" or "Machine Learning in Python"

I see these names often shared by my students obtained from online learning platforms asking me which is better. I honestly feel that these are a bit misleading.

Data Science is  a whole ocean of how you deal with data from visualization and mining to pre-processing followed by modelling to deployment. At each level, there are many tools which help you achieve objective

Machine Learning is a bunch of mathematical techniques to solve data related modelling problems. In R or Python ,the math is one and same. 

Learners please note : 

Concept should be learnt   Ex : ML, Inferential Statistics
Tool's capability should be assessed and then used to implement concepts  Ex : R or Python. 
Skill should be mastered by  practicing concepts with help of tools :  Ex : Data Science. 

Finally, post should be liked if it is meaningful :P

Content:
There is one quality which aspiring data scientists should cultivate.

It has many names but let me use the 'lemme'  - Idea Generation.

Most complex problems are solved by that one simple innovative 'idea' . It may be a new feature you generate or  ensemble or transforming regression to classification .. whatever !!

    So a good data scientist must be able to generate such ideas, implement , discard/deploy and iterate fast.

Whats happening for beginners now ?

    You learn from a course/textbook and do toy data sets. And you start and struggle on  kaggle or live datasets.

     This is equivalent to intialising weights of neural network randomly (courses/textbooks/toy datsets) and  predicting 'test' (live projs). The results will be pathetic because you didn't 'train' your 'neurons' for what you want (ideas) .

       If you give more ideas to neurons which I say is training , it will give back 'ideas' during test(live projs). Kaggle kernels, git and research papers give you  solutions/code where you can pick 'ideas'

PS : 'Good data scientists' in my network, don't ask me about validation ? . As you know, curves never fit perfectly, so are analogies. :P

Content:
Interviewer : What is your biggest strength ?

Me  : Perseverance 

I was expecting a question like "why do you think so" or "give me a situation" . But a different question came flying

Interviewer : Then what is your biggest weakness ?

Me : Perseverance 

Eye brows went up. Moved forward on the chair and 

Interviewer : How come perseverance is your biggest strength and biggest weakness at the same time ?


I replied, " Looking back, 70 % of times, I perserved , I succeeded. But rest 30 %, I failed. When I introspect, I feel , I should have spent lesser time on those 30 % of situations " 

I still don't know whether it convinced him or not . But yeah, deciding whether to push it forward still or give up on it so that you can focus on a different task is a difficult problem we face in research life. 

But the conclusion is  "Iterate fast".

Agree or Disagree ?
